study: Fixed axial dilation source-only intervention; established operation, no novelty claim
validation: next source user cyclically, four others train, held diagnostic only after weight selection
reused_control: shared128 from audited SWAD source pilot; ERM and fixed-tail states only
initialization: Identical seed2026 SignalNet weights and post-constructor RNG; only Conv2d dilation/padding attributes change
input: fixed legacy channels with no augmentation or auxiliary loss
scheduler: cosine over24 epochs, no early stopping
secondary_selection: earliest minimum validation CE including epoch0; no posthoc switch of primary
gate_rationale: Primary fixed-tail time2 must exceed baseline by0.5pp and axial range control by0.25pp, win at least4/6 vs each and lose no individual user by more than1pp vs either. Development screen only.
stop_on_failed_gate: No dilation/kernel/seed/window grid or eight-fold expansion for this fixed hypothesis. Do not generalize failure to all TCNs.
pass_next_step: Same-protocol eight-fold controls and independent seeds if warranted; scientific novelty remains separate.
persistence: All split IDs and each epoch exact order NPZ, model/AdamW/scheduler/RNG progress,24 segment averages, fixed-tail and validation-ERM states and logits; source/data hashes.
limitations: Six repeatedly researched development users, one training seed, overlapping train sets. GN and readout already use global spatial information. Axial dilation also changes sampling lattice and boundary padding; different time/range lengths mean this is not a perfect physical equivalence control. No calibrated range/velocity or global-RF claim. Not a reproduction of TCN or InceptionTime.
modified_layers: Only second stride-one Conv3x3 in each of three blocks. All stride-two convolutions unchanged.
factor_rationale: Dilation2 is the smallest integer expansion of unit spacing. Apply consistently to stride-one convolutions to keep learned downsampling unchanged. Chosen without candidate diagnostic scores; not optimized to measured event durations.
